summary: This note profiles community responses to natural disasters after September 1, 2023, including a 7.1 earthquake in Millersville, an Aster River flood in January 2024, and an August 2025 wildfire. It highlights individuals in preparedness, emotional support, education, technology, policy, and economic recovery, arguing that preparation, social ties, and reinvestment build resilience.
one_line: Profiles of people and communities coping with and rebuilding after earthquake, flood, and wildfire disasters since late 2023, stressing preparedness and resilience.
key_facts: A 7.1 magnitude earthquake struck eastern Millersville on October 17, 2023, turning the township into ground zero of a disaster.
Edwin Harper, 76, survived the Millersville quake and said, "The ground shook like it was angry."
The Aster River overflowed its banks on January 12, 2024, after relentless rain, affecting scores of neighborhoods.

Helena Springs, 55, a retired civil engineer turned disaster management consultant, was pivotal in orchestrating the flood emergency response; her earlier workshops on flood preparation had equipped the community.
In August 2025, drought conditions and an untended campfire led to a wildfire that consumed thousands of acres and threatened nearby residences.
Retired firefighter Jackson Parr, 60, led evacuation planning and community workshops, saying people remembered his fire safety programs and that "saved lives."
Post-fire rebuilding focuses on sustainable materials and incorporating firebreaks into landscape design.
Community organizer Isabelle Choi set up unity events across the city to promote collective healing, saying people need emotional support as well as physical rebuilding.

Martin Vasquez, a geography teacher at Central High School, added disaster awareness and mitigation to his curriculum with simulations, guest speakers, and collaborations with local disaster response teams.
Tech entrepreneur Priya Mehta created the Lifeline app, which provides real-time updates and guidance during crises.
Urban planner Raj Singh advocated for stringent building codes, which led to markedly less damage in vulnerable areas after recent disasters.
Financial advisor Laura Jimenez coordinates with local businesses and international donors and holds one-on-one sessions with small business owners to support equitable economic recovery.
